citations.narrative:
There were two loose guinea pigs hiding underneath a stack of transport enclosures in the “Old barn”. The guinea pigs
were easily caught by the licensee and were returned to their primary enclosures unharmed. Loose guinea pigs are at risk
for injury, predation, or loss. The indoor housing facility for the guinea pigs must be constructed so that it is structurally
sound and kept in good repair, to protect the animals from injury, and to contain the animals. Correct by ensuring the
primary enclosures safely contain the animals at all times. Correct by: July 1, 2026.

The facility is not cleaning and sanitizing enclosures as often as required to prevent accumulations of excreta and debris,
nor as often as necessary as described in the regulations. The licensee reported he is sanitizing enclosures every 4
weeks.
In the “old barn” there was one enclosure housing 16 guinea pigs in which the flooring was compacted dark brown fecal
material and other excreta and there was little to no identifiable dry bedding. Another enclosure housing 28 guinea pigs
had two dead juvenile guinea pigs that were in the early stages of decomposition. A third enclosure housing 5 guinea pigs
had one dead adult guinea pig that looked to have died recently.
Insufficient sanitization and removal of excreta and debris can serve as harborers of germs, can contribute to bad odors,
and may attract pests.
Correct by ensuring the primary enclosures are cleaned and sanitized often enough to prevent an accumulation of excreta
or debris, and that such enclosures shall be sanitized at least once every 2 weeks. Correct by: July 1, 2026.

The facility is not adequately cleaning the premises. In the "old barn" building used to house guinea pigs there are
numerous cobwebs observed throughout the facility including directly over and in between the stacks of guinea pig
enclosures. The cobwebs have an accumulation of trapped dust, debris, and bedding.
Failure to adequately clean the premises can lead to illness, transmission of diseases, create a fire hazard, and attract
unwanted pests. The facility must ensure that the premises are kept clean and in good repair to protect the animals from
injury to facilitate the prescribed husbandry practices set forth in this subpart.
Correct by: July 1, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Eric Irvin, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
